I'm approving T415 (91d2f6c0 against fe1508d3). It meets every acceptance item and changes no engine or web code. I didn't run any tests myself because this review session is read-only. The runner's own check passed: typecheck, lint, format:check and `vitest --changed` (98 files, 810 tests), all under the default config. The worker reports that worlds.test.ts also passes (4 tests) under the release-on config; the runner didn't run that, and I checked it by reading the code instead.

The risk reason was the autopilot decision of 2026-10-24 that is still waiting for the owner: every test names its release, and a release-on vitest config checks each file with the switch both on and off. The change follows that decision exactly, adds no new planning decisions, and only touches test setup, so it doesn't lock out the alternatives.

What I checked in the code:
- `DISABLED_RELEASE` and `ENABLED_RELEASE` are copies of the release object, so they keep their own on/off value whatever the switch is.
- `simulatedWorld(input, span, release = MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE)` puts the release in its cache ID and passes it through every nested build. The engine only reads the release in `createWorld` and the host constructor, and season rollover never reads it, so a world built with a given release stays on that release.
- `cached` reads `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled` when it runs and adds it to the key for both the memory and the disk cache.
- The engine's release object isn't frozen, and the setup file and the tests import the same object.
- `vitest.release-on.config.ts` merges the base config, which has no setupFiles, workspaces or projects. The tsconfig includes root `*.ts` files and allows `.ts` imports. The `package.json` script matches the acceptance text exactly.
- The cache-separation test flips the switch inside one case and restores it in `finally`. That is safe because cases in a file run one after another and the base config keeps each file in its own worker. The task notes say only the setup file should change the switch; this test-only flip goes beyond that, but the worker disclosed it, it is scoped to one case, and it proves the separation within a single run.

There are two optional suggestions and nothing that needs fixing.

findings.message: The global `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled` goes into every cache key, including `simulatedWorld` calls that pass an explicit release. Those worlds don't depend on the global switch, so the switch-off and release-on runs can't share them. That includes the `DISABLED_RELEASE` worlds that T417 will use for most shared engine worlds. Running both test tiers therefore builds and stores each of these worlds twice, which matters given the known problem of the world cache filling the disk. This follows the acceptance as written and doesn't affect T420's cold-vs-cold gate. Optional, for T420 to weigh against its warm timings: hash the effective release instead, i.e. the explicit one for `simulatedWorld` and the default for `cachedWorld`.

The test "simulatedWorld pins the release it is given" only covers a world on its founding day. If the release were dropped from the nested `simulatedWorld(…, release)` calls for seasons or rounds, the default would quietly take over, and none of the tests would catch it under either config. Optional: add a cheap case such as `simulatedWorld(input, { rounds: 1 }, DISABLED_RELEASE).matchModel` toBeUndefined, which fails under the release-on config if the release isn't passed down.

dispatch.summary: The rework fixes both P2 defects and closes all four P3s from the last review. (1) T422: a restart-phase sample counts as the kick only when the drawn ball is within SPOT_REACH (0.5) of the restart event's `from`. On the engine side, `from` is mirror(units(e.spot)) because restart trace entries carry no `from`, and the drawn ball is mirror(ballAt().at) in the same period. Both are in one frame, so the check holds for home and away. Saves don't persist frames, so only live engine frames reach it, unrounded. A delivery sampled in the air at a minute's end no longer ends the preparation; the new unit case 'a delivery sampled in the air at a minute end is not the kick' covers it. (2) tests/e2e/preparation.ts now seeks to a sample at least LEAD_SECONDS = 3 before the dead ball and starts the rAF recorder while paused. Only then does it click 1x, and it asserts that the first record is at or before `from`. Pitch.tsx matches what the helper assumes: slider onChange seeks and pauses, a speed chip calls setSpeed and setPaused(false), and each frame's elapsed is capped at 60 ms, which can only make drawnMs longer. (3) The `kind === 'restart'` filter is gone. Any event whose `restart` is a corner, free kick or goal kick counts, and the taker is read only from a restart entry's actor. A free kick or goal kick recorded as a foul or offside therefore takes its kick from the on-spot sample (new unit case). Throw-ins, kick-offs, penalties and dropped balls are still excluded, matching WEB-32's 'every free kick' and the earlier P3. (4) The opening journey now watches the seeded `stable-pace` pre-feature match. Its first-minute bound is presentationMs(0, first sample of frame 1, 2x, preparations), which is right because the minute label follows samples[sampleIndex].frame. The slack literal is now RECORD_SLACK_MS, the stale comment is reworded, and the owner hand-off sits in the T422 result. The base moved after the worker's last merge: 18db8f59 is not an ancestor. The only additions are T416 and T419 (engine test kits, tests and spec bookkeeping), with no overlap in app, e2e or engine sources, so the seeded matches are unchanged. The T421 work reviewed before (12000 ms minutes, 2x default, journeys reading the constants) is untouched by the rework. This verdict comes from reading the code. Two P2 defects block approval. (1) On the candidate model, when a minute boundary falls inside a set-piece delivery, the preparation runs past the kick: part of the delivery is drawn at the faster preparation rate, which breaks WEB-32 ("the kick and delivery play at the selected speed"). (2) The new browser helper starts recording after the clock has resumed, while the seek often lands only milliseconds of 1x play before the dead ball, so the new stable-controls journey is likely to fail in the batch run. findings.message: The fallback kick is 'the last phase:restart sample more than 0.1 s before the landing'. But the engine also gives the delivery flight phase 'restart': legsOf returns `phase: restart ? 'restart' : …` for spot entries, and knotted's flights use that leg phase. Every candidate minute also keeps a sample at its own end (instants keeps `to` = start+60). On the candidate the taker is never a holder before the kick (the kick knot adds a `rest`, not a `hold`), so the fallback is the main path there. Whenever a minute boundary falls between the kick and the landing, the minute-end sample becomes `to`. The kick→boundary part of the delivery (and the T359 kick sample) is then drawn at D/1500. At 1x a 25–30 s preparation makes that part 3–4× faster; at 2x, 1.7–2×. This breaks WEB-32 and the task goal ('nothing else on the timeline changed'). With deliveries of 0.15–5.6 s and about 70 prepared restarts per candidate match, this should happen about once or twice a match. Fix: count only restart samples where the ball is still on its spot (e.g. sample `ball` within a small tolerance of the restart event's `from`, which is its mirrored spot), or read the kick from the ball track. Add a unit case where a candidate corner's delivery crosses a minute end (restart sample at 60 with the ball off the spot) and assert that `to` is the kick sample.

findings.message: The helper seeks to the last sample at or before `from`, clicks 1× (which resumes playback), and only then starts the rAF recorder in a separate `canvas.evaluate`. On the pre-feature path there is always a sample at the ball going dead (P.times are kept), and the event's t is that time rounded to a tenth. About half the time that sample lies 0–0.05 s before `from`, which is under 10 ms at 1x. The first recorded `data-seconds` is then already past `from`, `enteredAt` is -1, and 'the clock reached the dead ball' fails. Even otherwise the margin is the gap to the previous sample (≈1 s of match time, about 200 ms at 1x), close to a click plus a CDP round trip. Seeds are fixed, so the new stable-pace journey would fail every time in the pre-push batch rather than flake. Seek to a sample a few match seconds before `from` (e.g. `times.findLastIndex(t => t <= from - 3)`), or start the recorder before clicking 1× and collect afterwards. Run the journey once on chromium before handing it to the batch.

kindOf checks the outcome before the spot. A restart entry whose delivery is flagged offside, or ends in a foul, is recorded as kind 'offside'/'foul' while still carrying `restart: 'freeKick'` (playback.ts sets ev.restart for any spot entry). Its actor is then the receiver or the fouler, not the taker. The `kind === 'restart'` filter skips these free kicks, so their preparation keeps running speed even though WEB-32 covers every free kick. The acceptance itself names `kind: 'restart'`, so this is a planning gap: either key on `event.restart` and resolve the taker another way, or record the exception in the task or SSOT.

The comment 'Every minute takes exactly 12 s at 1x, whatever happens in it' stopped being true once T422 added preparations. At 2x, a corner, free kick or goal kick preparation of 39 s or more inside the first minute would end '1′' before the 3.6 s check. That is rare but possible if the founding seed varies. Reword the comment, and either pick the first minute knowing it has no long preparation or derive the bound with presentationMs and the playback's preparations.

The recording slack is the literal `+ 1500`, the same value as SET_PIECE_PREPARATION_MS, which the impl note wants to stay the only preparation number. It reads as the preparation time. Name it as slack (or derive it from SET_PIECE_PREPARATION_MS) so the owner's later tuning cannot leave a stale twin.

Two autopilot decisions are waiting for the owner, as the risk flags note. (a) The kick is read from the taker's take or the last restart sample, not the restart event's t (the impl note's literal 'kick = the restart event's own time' would compress the delivery). (b) Measured match lengths are 14.3–15.9 min at 1x and 8.0–8.6 min at 2x, against WEB-32's 'about 13–14 / 7'. Neither blocks the code. Hand both to the owner's in-play review of SET_PIECE_PREPARATION_MS (ideation/match-viewing-pace-and-freedom) instead of changing the number here.

findings.message: Optional hardening. `played()` adds one incident to the grid's own incidents but does not check that the chosen player (`squads[side][1|2|4]`) has no later card or injury. The NPC-injury and ban cases also assume the grid added no injury or red of its own: they assert `out` has length 1 and `bans` equals one entry. Both hold for the 'settle-match' seed today. A change to the grid or to the seed could break these cases with a timeline error such as 'names X off the pitch' or an extra ban, and that failure would look like a settlement regression. Asserting these assumptions first, or choosing the player by them, would make such a failure easier to read. Not required for this task.

So the substitute-gain and fatigue cases play a different world depending on the switch. With the switch on, the comment's claim ("on the model a new career plays") is false. After integration this file would be the only candidate world that still follows the switch. Fix: merge the group base and change `modern` to `withCandidateModel(founded(2024, DISABLED_RELEASE))`. findings.message: The fallback kick is 'the last phase:restart sample more than 0.1 s before the landing'. But the engine also gives the delivery flight phase 'restart': legsOf returns `phase: restart ? 'restart' : …` for spot entries, and knotted's flights use that leg phase. Every candidate minute also keeps a sample at its own end (instants keeps `to` = start+60). On the candidate the taker is never a holder before the kick (the kick knot adds a `rest`, not a `hold`), so the fallback is the main path there. Whenever a minute boundary falls between the kick and the landing, the minute-end sample becomes `to`. The kick→boundary part of the delivery (and the T359 kick sample) is then drawn at D/1500. At 1x a 25–30 s preparation makes that part 3–4× faster; at 2x, 1.7–2×. This breaks WEB-32 and the task goal ('nothing else on the timeline changed'). With deliveries of 0.15–5.6 s and about 70 prepared restarts per candidate match, this should happen about once or twice a match. Fix: count only restart samples where the ball is still on its spot (e.g. sample `ball` within a small tolerance of the restart event's `from`, which is its mirrored spot), or read the kick from the ball track. Add a unit case where a candidate corner's delivery crosses a minute end (restart sample at 60 with the ball off the spot) and assert that `to` is the kick sample.

findings.message: The helper seeks to the last sample at or before `from`, clicks 1× (which resumes playback), and only then starts the rAF recorder in a separate `canvas.evaluate`. On the pre-feature path there is always a sample at the ball going dead (P.times are kept), and the event's t is that time rounded to a tenth. About half the time that sample lies 0–0.05 s before `from`, which is under 10 ms at 1x. The first recorded `data-seconds` is then already past `from`, `enteredAt` is -1, and 'the clock reached the dead ball' fails. Even otherwise the margin is the gap to the previous sample (≈1 s of match time, about 200 ms at 1x), close to a click plus a CDP round trip. Seeds are fixed, so the new stable-pace journey would fail every time in the pre-push batch rather than flake. Seek to a sample a few match seconds before `from` (e.g. `times.findLastIndex(t => t <= from - 3)`), or start the recorder before clicking 1× and collect afterwards. Run the journey once on chromium before handing it to the batch.

kindOf checks the outcome before the spot. A restart entry whose delivery is flagged offside, or ends in a foul, is recorded as kind 'offside'/'foul' while still carrying `restart: 'freeKick'` (playback.ts sets ev.restart for any spot entry). Its actor is then the receiver or the fouler, not the taker. The `kind === 'restart'` filter skips these free kicks, so their preparation keeps running speed even though WEB-32 covers every free kick. The acceptance itself names `kind: 'restart'`, so this is a planning gap: either key on `event.restart` and resolve the taker another way, or record the exception in the task or SSOT.

The comment 'Every minute takes exactly 12 s at 1x, whatever happens in it' stopped being true once T422 added preparations. At 2x, a corner, free kick or goal kick preparation of 39 s or more inside the first minute would end '1′' before the 3.6 s check. That is rare but possible if the founding seed varies. Reword the comment, and either pick the first minute knowing it has no long preparation or derive the bound with presentationMs and the playback's preparations.

The recording slack is the literal `+ 1500`, the same value as SET_PIECE_PREPARATION_MS, which the impl note wants to stay the only preparation number. It reads as the preparation time. Name it as slack (or derive it from SET_PIECE_PREPARATION_MS) so the owner's later tuning cannot leave a stale twin.

Two autopilot decisions are waiting for the owner, as the risk flags note. (a) The kick is read from the taker's take or the last restart sample, not the restart event's t (the impl note's literal 'kick = the restart event's own time' would compress the delivery). (b) Measured match lengths are 14.3–15.9 min at 1x and 8.0–8.6 min at 2x, against WEB-32's 'about 13–14 / 7'. Neither blocks the code. Hand both to the owner's in-play review of SET_PIECE_PREPARATION_MS (ideation/match-viewing-pace-and-freedom) instead of changing the number here.
